rationale: C20 is the immediate predecessor in the same supplemental-proclamation series and plausibly supplied both the language and operative architecture of the child. The child repeats C20's first four recitals nearly verbatim, updating only the chain of supplements; it then uses the same sequence of accession dates, activation of previously withheld Schedule XX concessions, consequential amendments to the Cuba list, and matching operative Parts I and II. The child expressly incorporates the list established by C20. C13 is a closely related earlier version of the same template, while C12 established the underlying Annecy Protocol machinery but is less directly congruent with the child's supplemental form.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Whereas by [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE] of December 22, 1949 ... I proclaimed such modifications ... which proclamation has been supplemented by [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE] of March 1, 1950 ... and [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE] of April 27, 1950
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Whereas by [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE] of December 22, 1949 ... I proclaimed such modifications ... which proclamation has been supplemented by [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE] of March 1, 1950
shared_material.explanation: The child carries forward C20's recital almost verbatim and merely adds C20 itself to the supplementation chain.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Whereas the trade agreement for accession ... has been signed by the following Governments under such conditions that it will enter into force for those Governments ... on the dates specified
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Whereas the trade agreement for accession ... has been signed by the Government of the Kingdom of Sweden under such circumstances that it will enter into force for such Government ... on April 30, 1950
shared_material.explanation: The child adapts C20's country-accession trigger from one government and date to several governments and dates.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the identification of each of the concessions ... shall ... be included in the list set forth in the ninth recital of the said proclamation of December 22, 1949, as supplemented by ... March 1, 1950, and ... April 27, 1950
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the identification of each of the concessions ... shall ... be included in the list set forth in the ninth recital of the said proclamation of December 22, 1949, as supplemented by ... March 1, 1950
shared_material.explanation: This is the same operative mechanism and phrasing, with the child extending the incorporated-list chain to include C20.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the list set forth in the ninth recital of the said proclamation of January 1, 1948, as amended and rectified, shall ... be further amended in the manner indicated in the ninth recital of this proclamation
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the list set forth in the ninth recital of the said proclamation of January 1, 1948, as amended and rectified, shall ... be further amended ... as indicated in the seventh recital of this proclamation
shared_material.explanation: Both use a separate Part II to implement consequential, item-specific amendments to the same Cuba tariff list.
